advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Inspect `rev-list ... --count` exit status and distinguish a proven-behind store whose count is merely unreadable (fail closed / re-derive) from a genuinely level store (fresh), rather than collapsing both to fresh via `behind <= 0`.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:108: `if _git("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", "HEAD", remote_ref).returncode != 0:` — reaching line 110 means HEAD IS a strict ancestor of remote_ref, i.e. genuinely behind, so a truthful count must be > 0

src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:110-112: `cp = _git(...); raw = (cp.stdout or "").strip(); behind = int(raw) if raw.isdigit() else 0` — `cp.returncode` is never checked; a failed rev-list yields empty stdout, `isdigit()` False, `behind=0`
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:113-114: `if behind <= 0: return None` collapses 'genuinely level' and 'count probe failed on a proven-behind store' into the same fresh verdict
run_git is invoked with check=False (freshness.py:100), so a failing rev-list returns a CompletedProcess with non-zero returncode and empty stdout rather than raising — the failure is invisible here

Ticket b251-cdca-c03e-4607 AC: 'the fix is to stop refusing on a NON-reason, not to make the gate more permissive when the store really is behind' — swallowing a failed count on a proven-behind store violates this
advisory.finding: The behind-count branch collapses two distinct worlds into 'fresh': a genuinely-level store (rev-list returns '0') AND a failed/unreadable count probe (non-zero exit or non-numeric stdout) on a store already PROVEN behind by the ancestry checks at lines 106-108. The exit status of `rev-list HEAD..remote_ref --count` is never inspected, so a count instrument that produced nothing on a proven-behind store now reports fresh.
scenarios: `git rev-list HEAD..origin/tickets --count` fails transiently (e.g. a remote-tracking ref that moved between the ancestry probe and the count, timeout, or git plumbing error) while HEAD remains a proven strict ancestor of the fetched ref
A gate certifies against a store that is genuinely behind because the count instrument returned nothing
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard on returncode/parseability: only treat as level when the count command succeeded and parsed to 0; when line 108 already proved HEAD is a strict ancestor but the count is unreadable, retain a behind verdict (the store is provably behind — fail closed), e.g. `if cp.returncode == 0 and raw.isdigit(): behind = int(raw); return None if behind == 0 else ("behind", behind)` and fall back to a fail-closed behind (e.g. count 1 or a distinct signal) on an unreadable count.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where rev-list returns a non-zero exit or empty/non-numeric stdout on a store proven to be a strict ancestor, asserting the intended (fail-closed) verdict.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py:119-120: the mock returns `subprocess.CompletedProcess([...], 0, "0\n", "")` — only the exit-0, literal-zero case
The `raw.isdigit()` False path (empty/garbage stdout) and the non-zero returncode path at freshness.py:110-112 have no coverage
advisory.finding: The added regression test only covers the clean '0\n' count path; it does not exercise the non-digit / failed-count case (empty stdout or non-zero returncode from rev-list) on a store already proven behind, which is the branch that silently swallows a probe failure.
scenarios: A future regression that changes count-parse or exit-status handling would not be caught by the current test set
